# NOW — the Chronicle

*Narrative only, regenerated by the engine from the page's records after every block (`saga.py record`); nothing here is edited by hand. Nothing from the real logs appears on this page except through the Reckoning.*

**BOOK I — THE HOUSE OF MENDERS · Chapter 4 — Old Mercy · the day after Old Mercy was said: the dawn answer, noon at the kennels, the afternoon in the hall**

- **Where:** Saint Ysolde's, the House of Menders; the infirmary hall, at the Captain's cot, with the hound under it.
- **The quest:** *The List.* The Confessors have come for the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's with a list: Darrow first, Hollis second. What stands between them and the hall is Old Mercy, the sanctuary bell: while it rings at dawn and dusk, no blade passes the gate and no name under it is taken down against its will. Marrant has not drawn a blade in a month. He has camped on the lower terrace, kept the cage, and reached into the House by the lever: a clerk in grey who never kneels sent two black slivers up in the House's own letter-satchel, one of them now set in the rock under the row and making the stone grow frost, and holds the almoner's sister at Calden for the second. Banners that are not grey are on the Holloway, a day off.
- **What Darrow is fighting right now:** The false letter is written and held: the second set, the hall quiet, in the almoner's own hand with every word's purpose told, and in it a brother's questions for his sister, where she is kept and a line in her hand, and one true line. It goes down with the carter and is read at the winch-house. If it is believed, the Confessor waits and the clerk may name the place; if it is caught, the next letter up comes without her mark. The answer at the dawn bell is owed under the Prior's roof.
- **Just happened (Scene):** *The Lymer.* A lay brother came down the row an hour later with a broom, stopped at the end of the Captain's cot, looked under it, and swept round.
- **With him:** Maelis Vorne (Gone back up from the kennels. She has seen the Captain's hand go to the drain grate and come away.) · Ser Hollis Garrow (In his chair by the brazier with the lad's blanket and the new cup strapped on, the Captain's hound under the next cot.) · Wren Ashdown (On the floor by the brazier with the ledger shut on her finger. She has shown the Captain how a letter down could work and asked him what it costs if caught; since *Three Answers*) · Ash (Under the Captain's cot in the infirmary hall on a new splint; the lay brothers sweep round her.)
- **Also here:** Ser Aldric Vane (Wrote again from Calden, before the list was read: Calden says the Ninth broke faith when its captain turned out of the line for one of his…) · Ser Benedek Orrin (Said his oath at the noon bell with Hollis's hand round his; the frost on his mouth neither grew nor melted.) · Brother Anselm (Heard the Captain say he has not stopped seeing the trowel in his hand, and every word of the letter and what it was for; asked what if it…) · Brother Cobb (Sat on a keg in the forge door taking the inside of Hollis's leather cup down a shaving at a time; told the Captain he was in his light and…) · Confessor Ivo Marrant (Stood behind his men's lymer on the terrace path below the kennels, said the hound was learning the House so it would know it again on the…) · Mother Ione (Came out of the chapel unasked and stood beside the Captain under the tower while he said the verse, then at the bars; told the Confessor t…) · Sister Pell (Came down the row between the dawn bell and the hour bell; read the Captain's mouth and made him say it plain; refused her hands with Ask t…)
- **The tales:** Tale 1 — Quickstep (1 of 3 told) · Tale 2 — Road's the Road (told in full)
- **Against him:** The Confessor's camp on the lower terrace, refused the almoner at dawn, with a lymer learning the House's scent.
- **Next:** The almoner's letter waits inside his shirt for the carter, and a grey hound sleeps under the Captain's cot.
- **Open choice:** none.
